subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - post-demo recap & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - post-demo recap & next steps

Jamie —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we covered:
- Performance: Redwood Dedicated can hit predictable p95 latency SLAs for generative workloads by using reserved GPU pools + dynamic batching and KV caching.
- Cost/Unit economics: with our batching + quantization recommendations we typically see 20-40% lower cost per token vs public hyperscaler inference for sustained workloads.
- Reliability: failover routing to a secondary region and capacity guarantees for reserved commitments.
- Integration: same API surface across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments — minimal app changes.

Open items you called out:
1) Baseline perf comparison vs AcmeCloud’s GPU endpoints at 10–20 qps, 2k token context.
2) Clarify commitment model for reserved capacity (terms, burst options, crediting).
3) Procurement: pricing and SOW for a 3-month POC with a reserved slice.

Proposed next tests (we can run these as a short POC):
- 1-hour sustained throughput test at 15 qps, 2k avg seq length (measure p50/p95/p99 latency and tail).
- Failover test: route 20% of traffic to a secondary AZ and verify latencies.
- Cost projection: run same request profile on our Dedicated config vs a mirrored run on AcmeCloud endpoints (we can coordinate with your infra team for keys).

I’ve attached a short comparison deck that highlights the dedicated vs hyperscaler trade-offs we discussed. Marissa (cc’d) will coordinate the smoke test and send a simple load script.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — can you confirm who on your side will own the procurement conversation and whether a 3-month reserved POC is something you can sign off on quickly?

— Markus
Markus Klein
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0189

From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmecloud.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - post-demo recap & next steps

Markus —

Appreciate the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick items from our side: 

- Procurement lead will be Evan Zhou (evan.zhou@acmecloud.com) — I’ll loop him in after I align internally.
- We’re particularly interested in how burst capacity works — our traffic has spiky daily peaks, and we need tolerable tail latency during those peaks. Can you send an example commitment table (3/6/12 month) showing reserved vCPU/GPU slices and burst pricing?
- For the baseline perf comparison we’ll need the load script and an SSH key or token to run from our test runners. We prefer the run to originate from our us-west-2 testers.

Also — can you share a rough price range for a small reserved slice (approx 1–2 nodes equivalent) so I can set expectations with Evan?

Thanks,
Jamie
Head of Platform Eng, AcmeCloud
jamie.liu@acmecloud.com
+1 206-555-0179

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-05T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - post-demo recap & next steps

Jamie —

I can run the smoke tests you asked for. Proposed plan and items we need from Acme: 

Plan (what we'll run)
- 60-minute sustained run at 15 qps, sample payloads (I’ll include a lightweight load script).
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token/sec, and cost estimate.
- Repeat with a 20% traffic shift to a secondary AZ for failover observations.

What we need from you
- Access: an API token for your test runner (time-limited) OR we can run load from our runners if you prefer.
- Representative model and prompt set (or tell us the model family + expected seq length distribution).
- Target SLOs (p95 under X ms) and any throughput constraints.

Burst/Commitment notes (quick primer)
- Reserved capacity = committed pool of GPUs (we size by vGPU units). Reserved terms (monthly vs annual) determine discount and guaranteed baseline throughput.
- Burst is priced as an overage rate that is lower for customers on committed contracts and higher for on-demand. We can share exact tables once Jamie confirms desired term length (3/6/12 months).

I’ve attached the demo recording and a small load script template to speed things up. I’ll provision the test cluster on our Dedicated staging env once we get your preferred test origin and token.

Attachments: demo-recording-20260304.mp4, load-script-template.sh

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acmecloud.com>, Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-06T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler GPU - post-demo recap & next steps

Jamie / Evan —

Great — thanks for the quick response. Evan, welcome — looping you in so we can align on procurement and SOW expectations.

Next steps / mutual action plan: 
1) Evan to confirm preferred term (3 vs 6 vs 12 months) and provide contact for legal/procurement.
2) Acme to share test origin (us-west-2) and either a temporary API token or permission for Redwood to run the load from our testers.
3) Redwood (Marissa) to run the 60-min sustained throughput test and share results (latency, cost projection, failover behavior).
4) Redwood to provide a provisional pricing table for 1–2 node reserved slices across 3/6/12 month terms plus burst pricing.

If that fits, I’ll put a one-page SOW + pricing on DocuSign for signature once we validate the perf numbers. We’ll also include a simple credit mechanism so unused reserved capacity in month 1 can be applied to later months for the POC.

I’ll aim to have the draft SOW and pricing to you by EOD Friday (2026-03-06) once Evan confirms term preference.

Thanks all — excited to run the tests.

— Markus
